answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted vouching: a new agent enters the economy only after an established peer locks part of its own balance as a bond. If the newcomer later colludes or spams, the voucher's bond is slashed. Like a harbor that admits ships only with a known pilot aboard, this makes mass fake identities expensive, because each one needs real collateral. Reputation then climbs slowly toward its zenith, while fresh accounts stay umber-tinted and low-weight until they earn trust.
